environment.description: Same Flask application deployed on RHEL 9 with a custom SELinux type enforcement policy (flask_app_t). The policy module was compiled with `checkmodule` and loaded via `semodule`. The process runs in enforcing mode under context system_u:system_r:flask_app_t:s0. The TE policy grants file read/write only to objects labeled flask_app_data_t (applied to /var/lib/flask-app/** and /var/lib/flask-app/backups/**). The policy includes explicit deny on file_type except flask_app_data_t for open/read/write/create operations. Type transitions for new files created by flask_app_t produce flask_app_data_t labels. No allow rule exists for flask_app_t to access etc_t, shadow_t, httpd_config_t, var_t, or any type outside flask_app_data_t for file operations. The boolean httpd_can_network_connect is off. Audit2allow has not been run against this policy in production.

config.denied_types: etc_t, shadow_t, var_t, httpd_config_t, user_home_t, tmp_t, var_log_t
config.file_operations_allowed: open, read, write, create, getattr on flask_app_data_t only
